title: shatter-arena widget params
description: A self-contained 'construct-to-break' arena for VC dimension / shattering. The reader places points in the plane and tries to SHATTER them with a hypothesis class: the engine enumerates all 2^m labelings (dichotomies), asks the author's realizes(plus, minus) predicate whether each can be realized by the class, and renders the verdict — SHATTERED if every labeling is realizable, otherwise it highlights the FORCED WITNESS (the actual ± split that no hypothesis can produce). Unlike a passive counterexample gallery, it evaluates the reader's OWN construction against a live predicate; placing a 4th point and discovering you can never shatter it is how the reader feels VC(half-planes in R^2) = 3. The renderer owns point placement (click to add, drag to move, click to delete), the all-dichotomies check, the witness highlight, the verdict + counts, and Reset; the hypothesis class is author-supplied via realizes(plus, minus). The gesture is 'construct-to-break' — building a configuration to break (or saturate) a claim against a live check. jsdom-safe: createSVGPoint/getScreenCTM run only inside the pointer handlers.

widgetId.description: DOM id for the outer <div class="widget"> wrapper. The Reset button derives its id from it.

svgId.description: DOM id for the <svg> drawing surface.

outputId.description: DOM id for the .readout (dichotomy counts, verdict).

hint.description: Optional hint in .hd > .hint. Should tell the reader to place points and try to shatter them.

svgTitle.description: Accessible <title> inside the SVG. Defaults to title.

className.description: Display name of the hypothesis class, e.g. 'a half-plane'. Used in the verdict sentence.

vcDim.description: Optional VC dimension of the class. When the reader has more than vcDim points and cannot shatter, the readout states the theorem (no set of that size can be shattered).

maxPoints.description: Maximum points the reader may place (caps the 2^m enumeration). Default 6.

initialPoints.description: Initial point positions in DATA coords (each [x, y]); the data window is [-range, range] on both axes. Default a single triangle of 3 points.

range.description: Half-width of the square data window: both axes span [-range, range]. Default 5.

bodyScript.description: Author JS. MUST define `function realizes(plus, minus){ return bool; }` — given the + and - point arrays (each an array of [x,y] in data coords) of one dichotomy, return whether some hypothesis in the class realizes it (e.g. for half-planes: whether plus and minus are linearly separable). Must return true when plus or minus is empty (the all-one-label dichotomies are always realizable). Evaluated once at render; must not start a timer or touch the DOM.
